points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` starts with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`. It then adds desktop-only pieces: the `electron-browser` contributions ... the node-backed services
`workbench.web.main.ts` also starts with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`. It then adds: `browser/web.main.ts` the web service implementations
`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` is the shared entry point ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` starts with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`
A service interface in `common` is often implemented twice, once in `browser` and once in `electron-browser` or `node`. Each entry file registers its own implementation through `registerSingleton`.
Only code referenced from entry point files is loaded.
Each feature has one `*.contribution.ts` file. That file registers actions, views and services as side effects. If an entry file never imports it, the feature is absent from that build.
